title: Right, acute, obtuse and reflex angles
summary: Classify and calculate angles using quarter, half and complete turns.
objectives: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or reflex from their measures.
Use complements, supplements and complete turns to calculate unknown angles.
Solve simple angle problems involving bisectors and related expressions.

blocks.text: Acute angles lie between 0° and 90°, a right angle is 90°, obtuse angles lie between 90° and 180°, and reflex angles lie between 180° and 360°.

An angle is the amount of turn from one ray to another, measured at the vertex. Read the smaller turn unless a reflex angle is explicitly marked. Acute angles lie between 0° and 90°, a right angle is exactly 90°, obtuse angles lie between 90° and 180°, and reflex angles lie between 180° and 360°.

Complementary angles total 90°, supplementary angles total 180°, and angles in a complete turn total 360°. Translate the geometry into one of these totals before forming an equation. An angle bisector divides one angle into two equal angles, so represent both parts by the same expression.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: A reflex angle is three times its smaller angle around the same point. Find both angles.

content.text: Let the smaller angle be x°. The reflex angle is 3x°.
Angles around a point total 360°, so x+3x=360.
Hence x=90, so the two angles are 90° and 270°.

sections.verification_note: The two results total 360°, and 270° is between 180° and 360°.

blocks.text: Do not classify an angle from the way a sketch looks. Use its stated or calculated measure. Do not call 90° acute or 180° obtuse: boundary values have their own names. For a reflex angle, confirm that the answer exceeds 180°.
